questions.question: Compare relational databases and NoSQL databases.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare relational databases and NoSQL databases.
  • ● Relational: Structured tables, use SQL, ideal for structured data.
  • ● NoSQL: Schema-less, supports documents/key-value pairs, good for unstructured data.
  • ● Scalability: NoSQL is better for horizontal scaling.
  • ● Flexibility: NoSQL adapts to changes faster.
  • ● Use case: RDBMS for banking; NoSQL for social media.
questions.final_answer: ● Use case: RDBMS for banking; NoSQL for social media

questions.question: Compare and contrast physical and logical database schemas.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare and contrast physical and logical database schemas.
  • ● Physical Schema: Deals with how data is stored physically (e.g., indexing, partitions).
  • ● Logical Schema: Abstract design (e.g., table structure, relationships).
  • ● Physical changes don’t affect logical design.
  • ● Logical schema is more user-focused; physical is system-focused.
  • ● Together, they define a complete data model.
questions.final_answer: ● Together, they define a complete data model

questions.question: Describe the historical development of biological databases.
questions.solution_html:
• ● 1970s: Start of GenBank and EMBL.
  • ● 1980s: SWISS-PROT and OMIM launched.
  • ● 1990s onwards: Growth of specialized databases like KEGG, DDBJ.
  • ● Emergence of NCBI as an integrative platform.
  • ● Shift from flat files to relational systems and web interfaces.
questions.final_answer: ● Shift from flat files to relational systems and web interfaces

questions.question: Relate the importance of data consistency, isolation, and durability in a database transaction. Illustrate with examples.
questions.solution_html:
• Relate the importance of data consistency, isolation, and durability in a database transaction. Illustrate with
  • examples.
  • ● Atomicity: Entire transaction succeeds or fails.
  • ● Consistency: Database moves from one valid state to another.
  • ● Isolation: Transactions occur independently.
